levels.title: First vowels and the K row

items.mnemonic: A crossed stem with a swirl below – hiding in the swirl is a lowercase a: a (father).
Two little strokes standing side by side – like the double i in Hawaii: i (ee, as in see).
A face in profile, lips pushing out to say oo – u (food).
A short flick above an energetic figure that twists and kicks out mid-exercise – e (end).
Like あ (a), but the swirl closes into a round o, with a small splash off the top right – o (go). The splash is the giveaway.
A leg mid-karate-kick, with a flick of motion beside it – ka.
An old key – two crossbars on a stem with a little curl below: ki (key).
An open beak pointing left – a cuckoo mid-call: ku (coo).
A barrel strapped to a post – a keg: ke.
Two short strokes stacked – two coins: ko.
き (ki) with one crossbar missing – count the bars: one for sa, two for ki.
A long lock of hair with a flick at the end – she has long hair: shi. Heads-up: the S row bends here, si becomes shi.
A vertical stem with a curl swirling round it – a straw stirring a drink: su (soo).
A wide mouth with a fang bending down at the right – it says se (set).
A single thread zigzagging down – sewing stitches: so (sew).
Squint: a lowercase t on the left, a broken a on the right – it spells ta.
さ (sa)'s mirror image – and the T row bends here: not ti but chi (cheese).
A low curling wave – tsunami: tsu. Another bend in the row: not tu but tsu (the ts in cats, plus u).
A tabletop with one curving leg – te (table).
A stubbed toe with a splinter sticking in – to (toe).
A cross above, a kneeling figure below – a nun at prayer: na.
A needle standing beside two stitches (こ) – ni (needle).
A tangle of noodles with a loop caught at the end – nu (noodle).
A cat sitting by a post, tail curled into a loop – ne, the first sound of neko (cat).
One smooth loop with a slash through it – a NO sign: no.
A capital H with a little a curled at its foot – ha. As the topic particle it reads wa (kore wa – as for this).
A single stroke swinging down and back up like a wide grin – hee!: hi.
Loose strokes drifting like puffs of air – the H row softens here: fu, a soft f blown between the lips, halfway to hu.
A low hill – you head up and over it: he (hen). As the direction particle it reads e.
は (ha) wearing an extra bar on top – ho.
Two bars crossing a stem that ties off in a loop – ma (mama). It's は (ha)'s right half with an extra bar.
A curling music note – a loop for the note head, a tail for the stem. Sing it: mi, as in do-re-mi.
A stem with a curled loop like a cow's nose ring – moo: mu.
Two curves crossing to make an almond shape – an eye: me (handily, me is Japanese for eye).
A hook with two crossbars – catch more with two barbs: mo (more).
A yacht heeling in the wind – a slanted sail with a pennant flying: ya (yacht).
A loop swinging right around a stem – a U-turn: yu (you).
A string with a yo-yo spinning at the end – yo.
A signal dash above a curled radio dish – ra (radio). The Japanese r is a light tongue-tap, halfway to l (like the quick d in buddy).
Two strokes side by side, the right one trailing long – a river between its banks: ri (river).
A zigzag road ending in a tight loop – a roundabout: ru (route).
ね (ne)'s twin without the loop – the tail just kicks up at the end: re (red).
る (ru) minus its end loop – ro. Loop = ru, no loop = ro.

levels.title: W row, ん, and the voicing marks

items.mnemonic: Same post as ね (ne) and れ (re), but the tail rounds into one wide open curve – wa (wide).
A twisting figure mid-cartwheel – を. Said as plain o, and used only as the object particle (hon o yomu – read a book).
One swooping stroke like a cursive n – n. The only kana with no vowel; before b, m or p it drifts toward m (senpai sounds like sempai).
Two small ticks at a kana's shoulder – switch your voice on: k to g, s to z, t to d, h to b. Two ticks = vocal cords buzzing.
A small circle at the shoulder – only the H row takes it, popping h into p. Think of the circle as a little bubble popping: p.
A shrunken や (ya) tucked at another kana's foot – the i drops and ya glues on: き + ゃ melts ki-ya into kya, one beat.
A small ゆ (yu) hanging low – same glue: the i drops and yu slides in, so し + ゅ is shu, one syllable.
A small よ (yo) at the foot – the i drops and yo takes over in a single beat: cho, kyo, sho.
A half-size つ (tsu) with no sound of its own – a tiny catch that doubles the NEXT consonant: き っ て = kitte, with a held beat before the t.
